summary: Uber's Q3 2023 earnings showed strong profitability gains but slower-than-expected growth, with revenue of $9.3 billion (+11%) missing the roughly $9.5 billion estimate. Ride-hailing and delivery drove improved adjusted EBITDA and a swing to net income, while Uber Freight dropped 27% in revenue and posted a loss. Shares rose 1.6% after the report as investors focused on year-over-year improvement and guidance.
one_line: Uber's Q3 2023 earnings beat on profitability, with net income of $221 million, but revenue and EPS missed estimates and Freight shrank.
key_facts: Uber reported Q3 2023 revenue of $9.3 billion, up 11% year over year, versus investor expectations of around $9.5 billion (FactSet, Refinitiv).
Uber posted Q3 net income of $221 million, or 10 cents per share, versus a net loss of $1.2 billion, or 61 cents per share, a year earlier; analysts expected 12 cents per share.
Uber guided Q4 gross bookings of $36.5 billion to $37.5 billion, up just 6% at the top end from Q3.
Total gross bookings rose from $29.1 billion to $35.3 billion, about 21%.
Ride-hailing bookings were $17.9 billion (+31%) and delivery bookings were $16.1 billion (+18%), generating $5.1 billion and $2.9 billion in revenue respectively.

Business model changes classifying sales and marketing costs as contra revenue reduced ride-hailing revenue by $161 million and delivery revenue by $360 million, together costing 8 percentage points of growth.
Ride-hailing segment adjusted EBITDA rose 43% to $1.29 billion from $898 million; delivery rose from $181 million to $413 million.
Corporate G&A and Platform R&D costs rose 5% to $595 million, and total adjusted EBITDA rose from $516 million to $1.09 billion.
Uber generated $394 million in operating income and $966 million in positive operating cash flow in Q3, all improvements on the prior year.
Uber Freight revenue was $1.3 billion, down 27% year over year but up 1% quarter over quarter, with an adjusted loss of $13 million versus a $1 million profit a year earlier.
Uber attributed the Freight decline to lower revenue per load and volume amid a challenging freight market cycle.
Freight rivals Flexport and Convoy struggled this year; Convoy shut down and its assets were acquired by Flexport.
Uber shares were up 1.6% in trading after the report.
